narrative.northStar: Starlight Stack — instrument panels in a night sky
narrative.overview: This is a developer portfolio built as a quiet, deep-indigo night sky. Real enterprise work floats as translucent blue-glass panels — instrument readouts lit from within — over a painted nebula and a drifting procedural starfield. The tech stack is drawn as a literal constellation: the owner's portrait is the brightest star at center, each core technology an icon node joined to it by faint lines. The world refuses both the flat white resume page and the generic dark-hero-with-gradient dev template; its materials (glass, backlight, starlight) are load-bearing, not decoration. The density is calm and centered, with generous vertical rhythm and a narrow readable measure for prose. Color is disciplined — the ground is near-black indigo, text is cool off-white, and the electric azure-to-cyan accent is spent sparingly on the one primary action and on active/hover states. Motion is restrained to one authored moment: the starfield twinkles, drifts, and parallaxes toward the pointer, and content rises once on load; all of it collapses to stillness under prefers-reduced-motion.
keyCharacteristics: Deep indigo night ground (#0b1026) carrying a painted nebula plus a live starfield
Translucent blue-glass panels as the primary material, lit not flat
A single electric azure-to-cyan accent, spent rarely
Inter for everything structural; Geist Mono reserved for data, status, and tags
The portrait-centered tech constellation as the signature device

rules.name: The One Bright Star Rule
rules.body: The cyan-to-azure primary gradient appears once per viewport — on the single most important action (Get in touch). Secondary actions are glass outlines, never a second gradient. The accent's rarity is what makes it read as light.

rules.name: The Ink-On-Night Rule
rules.body: Text is always one of the three ink steps on a night or glass ground; never pure #ffffff except inside ::selection and the skip-link. Accent colors label and illuminate — they do not set body copy.

rules.name: The Mono-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Geist Mono is used only for machine-flavored facts: status lines, role·period metadata, tech tags, and constellation labels. Never set a sentence or heading in mono.

rules.name: The No-Kicker Rule
rules.body: Sections and pages open directly on their heading. There are no eyebrow/kicker labels above titles; the eyebrow prop on SectionHeading and PageHeader is retained for call-site compatibility but deliberately never rendered.

rules.name: The Backlit-Glass Rule
rules.body: Panels are translucent navy glass — never opaque cards. Elevation comes from a hairline top highlight plus a far, soft shadow; a panel that needs to feel primary gets an inner radial backlight (.glass-lit), not a heavier drop shadow.

dos: Do build every content surface as translucent navy glass (.glass / .glass-lit) with a 1px azure-300 hairline border — not an opaque card.
Do reserve the azure-to-cyan gradient for the single primary action per view; make every other action a glass-outline secondary pill.
Do set all status lines, metadata, and tags in Geist Mono at 0.68–0.7rem, wide tracking, ink-muted.
Do keep text to the three ink steps on a night ground, and use violet-300 only for provisional/placeholder register.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: collapse the starfield and rise animation to stillness.
Do carry the global focus-visible ring (2px azure-400, 3px offset) on every interactive element.
donts: Don't add eyebrow/kicker labels above headings; sections open on their title.
Don't spend the primary gradient twice in one viewport, or use it for body text.
Don't use pure #ffffff for text (reserved for ::selection and the skip-link).
Don't convey depth with hard/opaque drop shadows; use the inner highlight + soft ambient + backlight vocabulary.
Don't set sentences or headings in the mono face, or use mono as a 'technical' costume.
Don't introduce a new hue family; extend within night / ink / azure / cyan / violet.
